title: Spaghetti Splatting: Differentiating Curvilinear Dirac Masses via Convolution
comment: 10 pages, 8 figures, 1 table
summary: In production systems, 3D geometry is represented by primitives such as points, lines, and triangles, as rendering hardware is optimized to generate images from them very efficiently. Learning such primitives from images by volume rendering is challenging, as they are Dirac masses defined at infinitesimal locations in space. EWA splatting, Poisson reconstruction, and 3D Gaussian Splatting overcome this by convolving Dirac masses with a low-frequency kernel, a recipe that generalizes along two axes: the kernel and the primitive. As points and triangles have already received significant attention, we investigate this recipe for curvilinear primitives, and introduce Spaghetti Splatting. We approximate curves by polylines whose convolution converges to that of the continuous curve, and volume render each segment so that connected segments composite without overcounting at their joints. For fast training and inference, we linearize the camera projection per segment, which also accommodates kernels beyond Gaussians, such as Beta kernels. As a point is a curve of zero length, our representation is a strict superset of 3D Gaussian Splatting. It remains competitive with the state-of-the-art on general scenes, outperforms methods specialized to line-like geometry, natively supports anti-aliasing, and produces long connected strands that are directly amenable to physics simulation.

Introduction sec:intro In production graphics systems, 3D geometry is represented by points, lines, and triangles~( , primitives), as rendering hardware is optimized to generate images from them very efficiently. Rather than constructing them by hand, we would like to optimize such primitives directly from a collection of images, by volume rendering~ mildenhall2020nerf and gradient descent. However, this is challenging, as primitives are Dirac masses defined at infinitesimal locations in space, so there is nothing for a gradient to act on. Research from about two decades ago showed us how to overcome this. EWA splatting~ zwicker2002ewa and Poisson reconstruction~ kazhdan2006poisson both turn a Dirac-like representation into a volumetric one by convolving it with a low-frequency kernel. This makes sampling the representation onto a discrete grid of pixels well posed from the perspective of the Nyquist--Shannon theorem~ yu2024mipsplatting . 3D Gaussian Splatting~ kerbl2023gaussians uses this idea to differentiate through point-like primitives, which it convolves with anisotropic Gaussian kernels. But could this idea be generalized? There are two potential axes of generalization, made apparent by the objective that these methods optimize: where is the image taken from camera viewpoint , volume renders the scene from that same viewpoint, and is the Dirac measure of the -th primitive, convolved with kernel . One axis generalizes the kernel, as in Deformable Beta Splatting~ liu2025dbs . The other generalizes the primitive, with initial research on convexes~ held2025convex , triangles~ held2026triangles , and, very recently, lines~ tojo2026lines . Note that the work by tojo2026lines is to ours. As points~ kerbl2023gaussians,yu2024mipsplatting,liu2025dbs and triangles~ held2026triangles,held2025meshsplatting have already received significant attention, we focus on differentiating through curvilinear primitives; see . To this end, we approximate curves by polylines, and show that their convolution with a kernel converges to that of the continuous curve as the segments shrink. Whereas the Gaussian convolution of a polygon requires evaluating Owen's T function~ owen1956tables,didonato1980polygons , the ray integral of a Gaussian-convolved segment only involves the Gauss error function~ ~( , the anti-derivative of a Gaussian). By volume rendering the density of each segment~ tagliasacchi2022volumerenderingdigestfor , connected segments composite without overcounting at their joints. For fast training and inference, we follow EWA splatting~ zwicker2002ewa and linearize the camera projection per segment, which also accommodates Beta kernels~ liu2025dbs . Our representation is a strict superset of 3D Gaussian Splatting, as a point is nothing else than a curve of zero length. As such, it matches or outperforms the state-of-the-art on Mip-NeRF~360~ barron2022mipnerf360 , , Deformable Beta Splatting~ liu2025dbs for geometry, coupled with Spherical Voronoi~ disario2026sv for modeling of view-dependent appearance. also outperforms methods specialized to line-like geometry: the concurrent work of tojo2026lines on their Fuzzy benchmark, and Gaussian Haircut~ zakharov2024haircut , which relies on hair-specific priors, on GeomHair~ lazuardi2026geomhair . It natively supports Mip-Splatting~ yu2024mipsplatting anti-aliasing, so it remains stable across viewing distances. Finally, our representation consists of long connected strands, which makes it amenable to physics simulation, and closer to what an artist would produce. We achieve these results through four key contributions: We note that the key ingredient behind 3D Gaussian Splatting and Poisson reconstruction, , convolving Dirac masses with a low-frequency kernel, provides a recipe that generalizes along both the kernel and the primitive. We investigate this recipe for curvilinear Dirac masses, and provide a convergent as well as efficient way to back-propagate through them. We generalize 3D Gaussian Splatting to a strictly larger family of representations, which remains competitive with the state-of-the-art on general scenes, while setting a new state-of-the-art for strand-based representations. We commit to to foster precise comparisons, and follow-up research. Related work sec:related Neural Radiance Fields~(NeRF) represents a scene as a continuous density and color field rendered by numerical integration along camera rays~ mildenhall2020nerf . Later neural fields addressed aliasing and unbounded scenes~ barron2021mipnerf,barron2022mipnerf360,barron2023zipnerf , while multiresolution hash encodings substantially reduced their training cost~ mueller2022instant . 3DGS replaced the neural field with explicit anisotropic Gaussians~ kerbl2023gaussians , and a tile-based rasterizer derived from point-based volume rendering and EWA splatting~ zwicker2002ewa,westover1990footprint . Subsequent methods have improved both its optimization and rendering. 3DGS-MCMC formulates population control as sampling~ kheradmand2024mcmc , and StopThePop introduces per-pixel sorting for more consistent visibility~ radl2024stopthepop . Other methods parallelize the backward pass over Gaussians instead of pixels~ mallick2024taming , integrate Gaussian density along each ray~ talegaonkar2025vol3dgs , render constant-density ellipsoids in closed form~ mai2025ever , or avoid the affine projection used by rasterization~ moenneloccoz2024threedgrt,wu2025threedgut . Another line of work replaces the Gaussian kernel: Deformable Beta Splatting~(DBS) learns the fall-off of a compact Beta kernel~ liu2025dbs , while Student Splatting and Scooping uses heavy-tailed kernels with signed weights~ zhu2025sss . Mip-Splatting prevents aliasing across viewing distances with a three-dimensional smoothing filter based on the training views and a two-dimensional filter during rasterization~ yu2024mipsplatting . Spherical Voronoi replaces spherical harmonics with a learned directional partition~ disario2026sv . We build on several of these improvements and adopt 3DGS-MCMC population control, the Beta kernel of DBS, Mip-Splatting filtering, and Spherical Voronoi appearance modeling. Beyond point primitives Another line of work replaces point centers with extended geometric primitives. Triangle Splatting~ held2026triangles and 3D Convex Splatting~ held2025convex optimize triangles and smooth convex bodies. Curve primitives have so far targeted sparse abstractions of a scene: 3Doodle optimizes 3D B\'ezier strokes and superquadric contours to render view-consistent sketches~ choi2024doodle , while SketchSplat reconstructs parametric 3D edges by splatting Gaussians sampled along curves onto multi-view edge maps~ ying2025sketchsplat . The concurrently developed line primitives of tojo2026lines are closely related to our work, as they also use line primitives directly for differentiable rendering. Their method rasterizes segments on a subpixel grid using the Bresenham algorithm and recovers high-quality geometry in object-centric scenes. That said, their line primitives are rendered at a constant screen-space width regardless of their depth from the camera, making the representation unsuitable for general scenes, as we show in our comparison on Mip-NeRF~360~( ). We include evaluations of our method on the Fuzzy dataset introduced by their work. Convolution surfaces A classical computer graphics technique, Convolution Surfaces~ bloomenthal1991convolution , has shown that one can represent many implicit shapes as an iso-surface of a convolution of a skeleton of curves and polygons with a smooth kernel. Recently, xu2025gpis demonstrated that one can efficiently render a Gaussian process implicit surface as an iso-surface of a sparse convolution of a kernel with randomly placed points. In both cases, the convolved field serves only to define an iso-surface. We instead use segment and polyline skeletons convolved with corresponding kernels as an explicit volume-rendering representation which we optimize from multi-view images. In this view, point-based splatting primitives are a special case of our segments with zero length, and our method maintains their fast rendering speed. Hair reconstruction Hair is a prominent example of geometry that is naturally described by curves. Neural Strands and Neural Haircut reconstruct strand geometry with learned priors~ rosu2022neuralstrands,sklyarova2023neuralhaircut . Gaussian Haircut and GaussianHair represent hair with Gaussians aligned to strand directions~ zakharov2024haircut,luo2024gaussianhair . Our reconstruction optimizes rooted polylines without a learned strand prior and passes the resulting curves directly to position-based simulation~ mueller2007pbd,mueller2012dftl . We use the public strand models from GeomHair lazuardi2026geomhair as reference geometry~ yuksel2026hairmodels . title: Plant Orbiter: 3D Plant Reconstruction and Generation with Video Diffusion Orbit Cameras and 3D Gaussian Splatting
comment: Submitted to Plant Phenomics. 16 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables
summary: Modern digital phenotyping pipelines require the precise measurement of a range of 3D morphological plant traits. The accurate, high throughput acquisition of these traits helps breeders and researchers accelerate the development of new varieties, techniques and products. Recent advances in 3D technologies have enabled a rapid transition from 2D to 3D pipelines, but high throughput acquisition of digital 3D twins of plants remains a significant challenge due to complex morphology, thin structures and occlusions. In this paper we present Plant Orbiter, a new approach to generating 3D plants that leverages recent advances in video diffusion to produce high quality 3D Gaussian Splats of plants from a single image. We show that our method more accurately recreates plant morphology than other state-of-the-art methods, achieving the highest 3D F-score against all baselines, while being more practical for high throughput pipelines due to easier alignment and reduced cost of camera placement. Combined with a 2D diffusion model, we show that our method also achieves state-of-the-art results in the generation of 3D plant models from a text prompt.

Digital Phenotyping 3D Reconstruction Monocular 3D Reconstruction Video Diffusion 3D Gaussian Splatting Text-to-3D generation Synthetic Data Introduction sec:intro Digital 3D phenotyping presents substantial advantages in crop understanding over existing 2D analysis tools. Non-invasive methods for extracting accurate morphology enables a deep understanding of plant health~ he2025multimodal , and can accelerate the development of new varieties, as well as providing better monitoring tools for growers~ hartley2023unlocking . 3D plant analysis unlocks many of the most important measures for growers, such as leaf area, and fruit volume while handling occlusion for dense canopies better than can be achieved with a single view. Within mainstream computer vision, the rapid development of 3D reconstruction~ mildenhall2021nerf, kerbl2023gaussians and generation~ xiang2025structured, zhao2025hunyuan3d techniques has already lead to widespread adoption of 3D models for both generation and analysis. Despite this, no current approach on plants achieves sufficient morphological accuracy, or the rapid acquisition, that would be required for the high throughput phenotyping pipelines at scale needed for agricultural settings. Existing methods in 3D plant capture often exhibit one of a range of limiting factors. Hardware dependant approaches such as laser scanners or robotic capture environments have high upfront costs, and are often low throughput. Multi-view methods like Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)~ mildenhall2021nerf or 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)~ kerbl2023gaussians directly learn a 3D representation from image sequences around a plant, but rely on computationally expensive camera recovery from structure-from-motion, which has high failure rates on complex biological structures. To tackle this, single image or monocular reconstruction methods have emerged in recent years to avoid the need for complex calibration of camera parameters. Image-to-3D generators~ hunyuan3d2025hunyuan3d, xiang2026native attempt to learn a direct mapping from a single image to a 3D model, but often suffer from poor performance on plants, and their output is challenging to realign and scale to the input image~ gao2026evaluation . Novel view diffusion methods~ chen2024v3d, voleti2024sv3d , such as one included in our own pipeline, have not previously been applied to challenging domains like plants. To improve the performance of reconstruction and other digital phenotyping tasks, the use of synthetic training data has proven increasingly popular due to a lack of available training datasets~ ubbens2018use,hartley2024domain . 3D data is often more challenging to produce and label, so this scarcity is even more pronounced and has motivated recent work in the generation of synthetic 3D plants using procedural and generative models~ hartley2025plantdreamer alongside wider research in text-to-3D models~ zhao2025hunyuan3d, yi2024gaussiandreamer . Despite recent advances, these methods suffer from high upfront costs, the need for hand-built per species rules, and in the case of generic models, poor performance on highly specific plant domains. In this paper we present Plant Orbiter, a versatile pipeline for 3D reconstruction of accurate, automatically aligned plants. We leverage recent advances in video diffusion models to produce an accurate, geometrically consistent orbital video around the plant based on a single input image, from which 3D Gaussian splatting can produce an accurate model. Our method both reduces the practical and computational costs compared to multi-image capture setups, and recreates plants with higher geometric accuracy compared to previous camera guidance methods ~ zhou2025stable, voleti2024sv3d . By prepending a text-to-image diffusion model to our pipeline, we also create a best in class model for the generation of entirely synthetic 3D plants that accurately adhere to a text prompt. We evaluate both the quality of synthetic plants but also the ability to prompt for specific phenotypic measurements, such as the number of fruits, and show that Plant Orbiter outperforms other leading text-to-3D models for both shape and prompt adherence. The contributions of this paper can be summarised as follows: A single image 3D reconstruction pipeline that achieves state-of-the-art geometric accuracy on reconstruction of plants. Experimental results for highly accurate height estimation from single image reconstruction, showing that video diffusion methods using our pipeline outperform 3D generation methods. A synthetic data generation pipeline that produces realistic synthetic plants, as well as experimental results showing our pipeline scores the highest for prompt adherence for phenotypical measurements. Related Work sec:related work 3D plant reconstruction. 3D plant reconstruction makes it possible to capture detailed, precise plant morphology traits and supports automated, high-throughput crop phenotyping~ li2025survey . 3D plants models have traditionally been obtained with laser scanning~ lin2015lidar , structured light or RGB-D sensors~ choi2024nerf , or from many overlapping photographs using structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo~ wang2025accurate . These approaches can be highly accurate, but they need dedicated equipment, controlled conditions and many viewpoints per plant. Plant structure also makes them fragile; thin leaves, overlapping organs and self-occlusion result in gaps and distortions in the reconstruction~ li2025survey,okura20223d . Neural radiance fields (NeRF)~ mildenhall2021nerf and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS)~ kerbl2023gaussians have since substantially raised the fidelity of plant reconstruction from ordinary photographs. While NeRF variants successfully model complex appearance without depth supervision, their implicit representation makes it hard to extract the explicit surfaces needed for trait measurement~ arshad2024evaluating,shen2025plantgaussian . 3DGS instead models the scene with explicit Gaussian primitives, which train quickly and render in real time, recovering traits such as plant height and leaf dimensions with accuracy close to laser scanning ~ stuart2025high,ma2026plant3r,yang2025gaussianplant . Robotic capture systems extend them to occluded organs and growth tracking ~ adebola2025botany, adebola2025growsplat . However, these gains in fidelity have not reduced the cost of acquisition, as current methods still require tens to hundreds of calibrated photographs of each plant. 3D generation from images and text. Generative 3D models learn shape and appearance from 3D training data that let them produce a complete object, including its unseen sides, from a single image or a text prompt. Because 3D training datasets are far scarcer than image-text pairs, early text-to-3D methods optimised a 3D representation for each prompt by distilling a pretrained 2D diffusion model through score distillation sampling (SDS)~ poole2022dreamfusion . GaussianDreamer~ yi2024gaussiandreamer applies SDS to 3D Gaussians for speed. MVDream~ shi2024mvdream distils from a camera-conditioned multi-view diffusion model, which reduces the multi-face artefacts that arise when each view is supervised independently. In parallel, image-conditioned methods learned to synthesise novel views from one image~ liu2023zero, shi2023zero123++, liu2024syncdreamer, long2024wonder3d and then lifted them to 3D in a single forward pass~ hong2024lrm, tang2024lgm, xu2024instantmesh . TRELLIS~ xiang2025structured decodes structured sparse-voxel latents into Gaussians or meshes from an image or a prompt, and TRELLIS.2~ xiang2026native extends this to open and non-manifold surfaces. Hunyuan3D 2.1~ hunyuan3d2025hunyuan3d first generates the shape with a diffusion transformer and then textures it in a separate stage, and DiffSplat~ lin2025diffsplat repurposes an image diffusion model to generate Gaussian splats. Multi-view image models generate only a handful of views, whereas video diffusion models, trained on vast real-world footage, learn how objects transform under continuous camera motion and can synthesise dense novel-view trajectories~ blattmann2023stable . SV3D~ voleti2024sv3d and V3D~ chen2024v3d fine-tune Stable Video Diffusion on rendered 360 orbits of synthetic objects, so that a single image yields a full orbit at known camera angles, to which a NeRF or Gaussian splat is then fitted. Later work improves the resolution and consistency of these orbits~ yang2024hi3d, zuo2024videomv,melas20243d, wang2026towards , and SEVA~ zhou2025stable extends them to arbitrary camera trajectories from one or more input views. Camera control can also be added to general-purpose video generators, either by injecting camera poses~ wang2024motionctrl, he2025cameractrl or by training lightweight LoRAs for specific camera motions~ sun2025dimensionx . VIST3A~ go2025vist3a skips explicit frames and decodes scene-level 3D Gaussians directly from the latents of a text-to-video model. These models are trained mainly on synthetic 3D assets~ deitke2023objaverse and evaluated on general objects, and plants, with their thin, overlapping and highly variable organs, expose the limits of this training~ hartley2025plantdreamer, gao2026evaluation . Single-image methods built for plants do exist, but they mostly target trees and rely on hand-designed botanical priors~ li2021trees, li2024svdtree, lee2024treedfusion, liu2025hierarchical . From text, general 3D generators also offer little control over specific plant traits, such as the number of fruit, whereas text-to-image models, trained on far more data, follow such detailed prompts much more closely~ zhao2026qwen . Our aim is therefore to generate 3D plants that are faithful to an input image or text prompt, leveraging the priors of existing text-to-image and video diffusion models without requiring specialised 3D plant training data.
